_comment: Functions that ARE compiler output and should match, but have not yet.
They are held out of the work queue so waves stop rediscovering them,
and they are deliberately NOT counted as progress anywhere: a parked
function is still assembly, the ROM is still built from its asm/ unit,
and the C in work/<fn>/ does not go into src/decomp/.
This is a different claim from data/asm-resident.json. That file says
'no C will ever match this, because a compiler did not write it'.
This file says 'C should match this and ours does not yet'. Do not put
an entry here in asm-resident.json to get it out of the queue -- that
file is the evidence base for what hand-written assembly looks like,
and a wrong entry poisons every later judgement made from it.
An entry needs three things: the best percentage reached, the EXACT
remaining difference, and the axes already ruled out. Without the
ruled-out list the next wave repeats the same attempts -- which is the
specific failure this file exists to prevent.
TWO SHAPES ARE ACCEPTED and both are read as opaque by index_functions.
Older entries are a single prose string. PREFER THE OBJECT FORM for new
entries -- sub_0804FA2C is the worked example -- because it makes the
ruled-out list a real list instead of a sentence buried in prose:
bytes, best, remaining_diff, why_it_is_close,
axes_ruled_out[], settled_by_this_attempt[], reason
`settled_by_this_attempt` is the one that pays: it names derivations the
attempt PROVED, so an unpark does not re-litigate them.
Before parking anything, check the toolchain axis. The ROM was built
with two compilers and more than one flag set, and three functions were
parked as source-exhausted across two waves and permuter runs when the
source was never the axis. See data/compiler-overrides.json and the
'Per-file compiler and flags' section of docs/agbcc-codegen.md.
Unparking is the goal. Re-run `python tools/trymatch.py <fn>` against a
parked entry whenever a new codegen rule lands; the draft is kept at
work/<fn>/<fn>.c and best.c holds the closest attempt.
THE .rodata WALL IS GONE (wave 18, W18-B). Twelve entries here used to say
're-test when the split can express a .rodata word'. It can now. agbcc parks
a -fforce-addr address constant in the compiling unit's own .rodata, and in
this repo those same bytes also arrive as incbin'd ROM data in data/rodata.s
or data/data.s -- so a byte-exact honest draft could not be promoted, because
its word had nowhere to live and the blob was still supplying it.
tools/split_rodata.py now splits those blobs per symbol into generated pieces
under build/rodata (reading data/, never modifying it, exactly as
split_asm.py treats asm/), and gen_lds.py interleaves a promoted unit's own
.rodata between the pieces at the address the original build used. Declare
the words a unit owns with a `rodata` list in data/promoted.json.
ALL TWELVE were unparked this way -- sub_080081E0, sub_080083E0,
sub_0800977C, sub_0804E8F0, sub_0804FE10 and the seven-member sub_0805CA60
group, 3,368 bytes -- every one from a draft that names the global DIRECTLY,
with both builds reproducing the SHA1. See docs/agbcc-codegen.md.
COROLLARY, and it matters for what you keep in work/: when the honest
spelling is byte-exact and only its relocation differs, THAT draft is the
deliverable and the c_local workaround is not. Keep the honest one as
work/<fn>/<fn>.c. Three functions were held parked for several waves by
grinding on the workaround's register allocation when the honest draft had
been byte-exact the whole time.
DO NOT relax trymatch's reloc_equivalent to bless a .rodata word without
checking the placement exists. trymatch judges one unit; the split build
links all of them. A promoted unit whose .rodata the linker script does not
place either loses the word or shifts every address after it, and because
promote.py acts on trymatch's verdict the failure lands in the build with
functions already moved. Placement first, verifier second.

FORMATTING: this file is written with json.dump(..., indent=1). Dump it with any other indent and every line churns in the diff, which buries the one entry you added -- wave 26 did exactly that and had to redo it. LINE ENDINGS TOO, and the two data files DISAGREE: this file is CRLF, data/asm-resident.json is LF. json.dump writes '
', so open this one with newline='
' -- writing LF here churns all 394 lines exactly the way a wrong indent does, and hides the one entry you changed. Wave 28 hit it and caught it only by running `git diff --ignore-all-space --stat` when the diff looked absurd. Do that check before committing either file.

sub_0804EB78.best: 80.1% identical, 112 of 564 differing bytes, first difference at +0xa. Re-measured wave 73 (W73-E) with `trymatch.py` on the DRAFT itself (`new best: 80.1%`), not on best.c.
sub_0804EB78.park_kind: EXTRA SPILL SLOT IN A SIZE-EXACT COSTUME -- not a pure register-name residual
sub_0804EB78.remaining_diff: THE SIZE-EXACTNESS IS FAKE and this is the wave-73 brief's `sub_08045FC8` warning realised at 564 bytes. `size: match (564 bytes)` and `size_delta: 0`, but the candidate's frame is FOUR BYTES LARGER than the ROM's -- the tail reads `add sp, #48` against the ROM's `add sp, #44`, and every spill displacement is shifted by 4 ([sp,#20]/[sp,#24]/[sp,#44] against the ROM's [sp,#16]/[sp,#20]/[sp,#40]). The candidate carries ONE MORE SIMULTANEOUSLY LIVE VALUE than the original and spills it; the section still measures 564 because the extra code bytes are absorbed by literal-pool alignment padding. So the residual is an EXTRA STORE/RELOAD PAIR, i.e. wave 37's `one extra instruction` class -- the one class the permuter is documented as unable to reach -- and NOT the pure register-name class it superficially resembles. VERIFY THE FRAME SIZE, NOT `size: match`, before treating this function as size-exact.
sub_0804EB78.why_it_is_close: Every call, every branch, the whole `req` block, the 180-byte group stride, the *36 entry stride and the three `-fforce-addr` .rodata address constants are present and in the ROM's order. The 80.1% is positional: the first difference at +0xa is downstream of the frame being 4 bytes wider.
axes_ruled_out: Wave 37 (W37-J), recorded in the draft header: `gUnknown_085534C4[(c * 5 + f) * 2]` is WRONG and `[c * 10 + f * 2]` is right -- the factored spelling creates `c * 5` as the CSE'd subexpression and drags gUnknown_02029B94[c][e] into `(c * 5 + e) * 2` as well.

Wave 37 (W37-J): the final sub_080155C0 entry MUST be `(e3 = <expr>)->x` inside argument 1. As its own statement the entry is computed BEFORE gUnknown_03001FBC is loaded; inlined twice in arguments 1 and 2 the multiply comes out as `adds r2,r7,#0; muls r2,r1` instead of `movs r1,#0xb4; muls r1,r7`.

Wave 37 (W37-J): `p = *(u16 **)(c * sizeof(u16 *) + (u8 *)gUnknown_084C3F78)` rather than `gUnknown_084C3F78[c]` -- the byte-offset-first spelling puts `lsls #2` before the pool `ldr`, which is what the ROM does. This one closed sub_0804F0D8 and sub_0804F8BC outright.
Wave 37 (W37-J): `(row = gUnknown_02028E5C[c])[1]` rather than `gUnknown_02028E5C[c][1]` -- the `[][2]` subscript reassociates to `base + 2 + c * 4` and hoists the +2 out of the load displacement.
Wave 37 (W37-J): `volatile u16 unk20` on the struct member, probed directly -- it emits a THIRD `ldrh` before the store, which the ROM does not have.

Wave 66 (W66-D): a read-site-only volatile cast restores exactly the missing post-store `ldrh` without the third load a volatile member causes, and replacing the entry pointer arithmetic with array syntax adds a spill. Neither closes the function.

Wave 73 (W73-E): DELETING THE `volatile unsigned int new_var2` LOCAL AND THE `unsigned long new_var = sizeof(...)` ALIAS, writing `gUnknown_08552148[c]` plainly at both use sites. This was the obvious read of the extra stack slot and it is WRONG: 80.1% -> 60.6%. The plain re-read DOES restore the ROM's reload of gUnknown_08552148[c] (`ldrh r2,[r5,#0]` twice, the *36 shift chain re-expanded each time, no [sp,#16] slot for that value), but the frame stays at 48 and the whole r8/r9 assignment inverts, so the value cached in that slot is NOT the source of the extra slot. The volatile local is buying something real; do not tidy it away.

Wave 73 (W73-E): reading `164/168/16c: R_ARM_ABS32 .rodata +4/+8/+0` against the ROM's `gUnknown_08136094/98/9C` as a residual. It is a SYMBOLISATION difference of the same kind as the branch-label case -- these are agbcc's own `-fforce-addr` address constants for &gUnknown_03001FBC, &gUnknown_02029A10 and &gUnknown_02029B94, verified against baserom.gba in wave 37, and split_rodata carves them at promotion. Do not chase them.
settled_by_this_attempt: Wave 73 (W73-E): the residual is +4 bytes of FRAME, not a register permutation. Measure `add sp, #N` in both streams before classifying any large parked function as a pure register-name near-miss -- `best.json`'s `exact_size: true` and trymatch's `size: match` both report the SECTION size and are blind to pool-padding compensation.

Wave 73 (W73-E): this function had NO parked.json entry at all before this wave despite two waves of measured work; the whole ruled-out list above was living only in the draft's file header. Grep the draft header before concluding an axis is untried.

sub_08014DCC.remaining_diff: A PURE REGISTER-NAME residual: same size, same instruction count, same branch structure. The ROM keeps p and next in the SCRATCH pair r2/r3 and spends r4-r7 on size, bestSize, total, best and bestNext; the candidate keeps p in r1, size in r2 and bestSize in r3, so it needs one callee-saved register fewer and its push mask is {r4,r5,r6,lr} against the ROM's {r4,r5,r6,r7,lr}. That is why first difference is +0x0 -- the prologue is the LAST symptom, not evidence about the frame.
sub_08014DCC.why_it_is_close: Every statement of the body, the 16-byte header {next,size,used,filler}, the tail layout and the loop's basic-block structure are the ROM's. The two missing instructions wave 42 recorded are gone.
axes_ruled_out: Wave 42 (W42-D): four loop shapes that all COALESCE `p = next` -- `while (1) { body; next = p->next; if (!next) break; p = next; }`; `for (;; p = next) { body; next = p->next; if (!next) break; }` (gcc canonicalises these two together); the same with an explicit `goto` INTO the loop past the copy (optimised away, no effect); `do { body; next = p->next; p = next; } while (next != NULL);`.

Wave 42 (W42-D): the fixpoint it shipped -- `next` seeded before the loop with `p = next` as the first body statement. Keeps p and next apart but runs the copy on the first iteration too, which IS the -4. Superseded by the wave-73 draft.

Wave 73 (W73-C): basic-block PLACEMENT is not what is left. The ROM places the latch physically AHEAD of the header so the back edge falls through, and pays `bne <header>; b <ret0>` at the guard; the candidate falls into the header and pays a `b` at the loop bottom. Seven instructions either way -- the two layouts cost the same.

Wave 73 (W73-E): THE HANDOFF WORKED AND IT IS THE BATCH'S CLEAREST RESULT. W73-C predicted that making the function size-exact moved it out of the permuter's provably-useless class (one extra instruction) into its documented sweet spot, and that chained runs had never been tried from that state. Run 1, `--current` from the 10.0% draft: 10.0% -> 63.33%, size-exact, semantically clean, INSTALLED AS THE DRAFT. Runs 2 and 3, chained: 65.83% and 68.33%, BOTH SEMANTICALLY WRONG. Run 2 -- it moved `new_var = p->size;` inside the if-body while the guard still reads `new_var`, so the guard reads an uninitialised value; run 3 ended the function `return (void *) total;`, where `total` is `size + 0x10` on both NULL-returning paths, not 0. NEITHER was adopted as written -- but run 3 was worth READING: correcting that one return to `return (void *) 0;` and keeping its other three mutations (`total = size; total = total + 0x10;` split, the hoisted load reverted, `total = 0; q->used = total;`) gives 70.0%, which is the current draft and the final state. 10.0% -> 70.0% in one wave. Wave 42's negative was against a MISSING-INSTRUCTION residual, exactly as W73-C said. NOTE THE TOOLING TRAP: best.c held the wave-42 body 4 bytes short, so the MCP `permute` tool -- which always starts from best.c and cannot pass `--current` -- would have searched the wrong starting point. Shell out to `python tools/permute.py <fn> --current` whenever the draft beats best.c. ALSO MEASURED AND NOT TO BE REPEATED: deleting `new_var2` and using `size` directly at all three sites costs FOUR BYTES (120 -> 116, 13.3%) and drops r7 from the push mask -- that local is buying a register, not redundant. THE NEXT PROBE is `q->used = (u32)next;`: the ROM writes that field with `str r3,[r2,#8]` where r3 still holds `next`, which is provably NULL at _scan_done since the label is only reached by the `next == NULL` goto. Wave 42 called that reload_cse and not something to author, but it reuses `next`, not a zero constant, so the probe is semantically valid and has never been run. DO NOT GENERALISE THE REPAIR FROM THIS FUNCTION: it is the 1 of 3 that worked. The same technique returned the baseline score on sub_0800E9F4 and on W73-B's sub_08045C18. It works here only because the invalid part -- a wrong return value -- was INCIDENTAL to the live ranges the other three mutations created.

WAVE 77 (W77-G): THE `NEXT PROBE` THIS ENTRY AND THE DRAFT HEADER BOTH NAMED IS NOW MEASURED AND IT IS NEGATIVE. The tail hunk is ROM `adds r2,r0,#0 / str r6,[r2] / subs r0,r4,r7 / str r0,[r2,#4] / str r3,[r2,#8]` against the candidate's `str r6,[r0] / subs r1,r4,r3 / str r1,[r0,#4] / movs r3,#0 / str r3,[r0,#8]` -- five instructions each, the ROM spending a copy of q into r2 and reusing r3 (= next, provably NULL at _scan_done) for the `used` store where the candidate spends `movs r3,#0` and keeps q in r0. Writing the store as `q->used = (u32) next;` does NOT buy the ROM's reuse: it goes 120 -> 116 bytes (-4, 50.0%), i.e. gcc drops TWO instructions rather than one. The zero is const-propagated through `next` and the candidate loses the materialisation without gaining the copy. The `movs r3,#0` is not a missed reuse opportunity -- it is what pays for keeping q in r0, and the two spellings are a package.
settled_by_this_attempt: Wave 73 (W73-C): THE LEVER IS `goto` INSTEAD OF `break` FOR A TRAILING EXIT TEST. `while (1) { body; next = p->next; if (next == NULL) goto _scan_done; p = next; }` puts the copy in a real latch block AND does not coalesce. This is the wave-59 sub_08029AF8 lever (a user goto is not a jump to the loop's own end_label, so expand_end_loop does not roll the exit) applied to a TRAILING rather than a LEADING exit test. Contrast sub_08014DCC, where the same repair technique on an invalid 68.33% body yielded 70.0% and a new best because three of its four mutations were sound. WAVE 73 (W73-G): DEFINING `dst` IN THE OUTER BODY *AND* REDUNDANTLY AT THE END OF THE INNER BODY -- the one spelling that looked like it reached both ends of the span. It reaches neither. The two pool words survive, but the inner def is NEITHER HOISTED NOR DELETED (it sits at the loop bottom costing two instructions an iteration) and the outer def still lands ahead of the zero-trip guard. The reason is a precondition of gcc's move_movables this project had not recorded: A MOVABLE'S REGISTER MUST NOT BE LIVE ON ENTRY TO THE LOOP. Defining dst anywhere outside the inner loop makes it live at entry and FORECLOSES THE HOIST BY CONSTRUCTION, so no outer position can ever work and the whole `where outside` axis is closed. gpKeySt getting an ORDINARY inline pool word while the other three globals get force-addr words, in the same function, is the reference-count trigger and not something to spell differently.

LEVER 2, `base - (-index)` (wave 73, W73-F): NEGATIVE, and the reason generalises. Writing the 0xc0 block's address as `q = (u8 *)&gUnknown_03003FC0 - (-*(s16 *)&ent->unk38);` forces `ent` to be computed before `q`, which MOVES the force-addr pool load for gUnknown_03003FC0 from the head of the block (where the ROM has it, `ldr r2,[r5]` is the block's first instruction) to after the element-address computation. And it buys nothing, because the additive spelling ALREADY has the symbolic base as operand 1 and as the destination: the ROM is `adds r2, r2, r0` and the draft reproduces that. THE GENERAL RULE: read the ROM's address add before reaching for lever 2 -- it is indicated only when the ROM has the symbolic base as operand 1 AND your candidate has it as operand 2. Here the operand order was never the residual.
